Thirteenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica, Scientific Report, 1997 
Department of Ocean Development Technical Publication No. II, pp. 389-393 
Medical Care for the Expedition 
SUBRATA DAS 
Medical Attendance 
A total of 530 cases have been managed since 8 Dec' 93 till 28 Mar' 95, onboard 
MVStepan Krasheninnikov, at Maitri, and onboard MVPolar Bird. Most of the 
cases barring a few major ones have been minor. All the cases have responded 
well to treatment. The number of cases involving injuries, including cold 
injuries, sprains, and strains have been high, in comparison to the last team. No 
effort has been spared to provide the best medical care promptly, and within 
the available resources.

Status of Medical Stores 
A thorough check of all stores were carried out, unserviceable items 
separated and those not on charge, taken on charge. Most of the electrical / 
mechanical apparatus were serviced and some unserviceable ones recondi-
tioned. Expired drugs / chemicals backloaded. 
Health Check-up 
Quarterly medical check-ups were carried out for Army personnel. A 
constant watch was kept on the health status of all members, and necessary 
advice / treatment given, as and when required. 
Reorganisation of Clinic / OT 
The clinic and OT were revamped with available resources. Non-essential 
items were removed to the loft for storage in view of the scarcity of the space. 
Radiography 
Acknowledgements 
A total of 15 X-rays were taken despite the limitations due to cramped 
confines of the clinic, non availability of proper X-ray cassettes, expired X-ray 
films, and vertical cassette holder. 
Cooperation with Novolazaravskaya Station 
Dr. Boris Derjadin of Novolazaravskaya Station has been of immense help 
and assistance for management of Dental Cases, Mutual consultations for 
management of patients were done, as and when required. 
Cooperation with AIIMS 
The responsibility of Medical Care and the research on Human Physiology 
was borne jointly by Dr. Arun Joshi of AIIMS, and self. I am grateful to him 
for conducting biochemical tests, specially LFT for a case of Viral Hepatitis 
and a case of Pulmonary Tuberculosis. His assistance for conducting surgery 
was excellent. 
Cooperation with XIV ISEA 
All members of the XIV Expedition stationed at Maitri were provided 
Medical Care till the Surgeon and Anesthetist of the new team were inducted. 
I am grateful to Sqn Ldr S Anant for giving General Anesthesia onboard MV 
Polar Bird
